Healthcare waste is crushing taxpayers. Look at the numbers: Ambulatory Surgery Centers deliver procedures at 55% of hospital costs. Yet Medicare keeps overpaying hospitals by 82% for identical surgeries.

That's $2.6 billion in taxpayer dollars vanishing into bloated hospital systems annually. Not theoretical waste—real money that could fund better care for patients who need it most.

The solution isn't complicated. Cut the bureaucratic markup, redirect funds to efficient providers, and track every dollar. When ASCs can do the same procedure for half the cost, paying hospital premiums isn't just wasteful—it's negligent.

Accountability in healthcare spending isn't a suggestion. For millions of patients waiting for care, it's the difference between getting treatment now or getting waitlisted by overpriced systems.
